fixtures.rationale: The function increments and reads a module-level let that is not passed in, so its result depends on hidden state.
The function mutates a module-level array by pushing into it and returns that shared array as its result.
The function mutates a field on a module-level object instead of receiving and returning a new value.
The module-level Map is used as a registry whose stored counts change on every call, so the function's result depends on and changes shared state.

setRegion reassigns a module-level let at runtime, changing what every other function that reads activeRegion sees. Both setRegion and currentRegion reference the binding, so the rule produces one candidate per function.

isUnderMaintenance's result depends on a module-level let that a different function toggles, so it reads hidden state even though it never writes it. Both setMaintenanceMode and isUnderMaintenance reference the binding, so the rule produces one candidate per function.
MAX_RETRIES is a fixed numeric constant that is only ever read, never reassigned or mutated.
The lookup table is frozen and only read, so it behaves as a fixed constant rather than mutable shared state.
The module-level regex is a fixed pattern reused across calls and never mutated.
The config object's fields are only read to build a string; nothing in the function reassigns or mutates apiConfig.
The Map is module-level state written on a miss and read on a hit; a cache is a deliberate exception to the rule, recorded with an inline suppression, not something the rule allows.
The Map is module-level state that changes with every miss and decides what later calls return; caching is an exception to the rule, recorded with an inline suppression.

getDefaultLogger both writes the module-level let on first call and reads it on every call, and the singleton it hands back is the same shared instance no caller chose to inject; that is hidden state, not a pure cache of one function's own computation.
The filename matches the default test file pattern, so the rule produces no candidates at all regardless of its contents.
greet never references the module-level callCount binding, so the function has no hidden-state candidate at all.
